item.title: The Global Lakes Explorer: a basin-to-global scale data visualisation application for the assessment of nutrient emissions to lakes
item.dc:title: The Global Lakes Explorer: a basin-to-global scale data visualisation application for the assessment of nutrient emissions to lakes

Spears a UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology, Edinburgh, UKb School of GeoSciences, The University of Edinburgh, Edinburgh, UKc Department of Earth Sciences, Faculty of Geosciences, Utrecht University, Utrecht, The Netherlandsd Department of Integrated Environmental Policy Analysis, PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency, The Hague, The Netherlandse Ministerio del Medio Ambiente de Chile, Santiago, Chilef Lehrstuhl für Ingenieurhydrologie and Water Management, Ruhr University Bochum, Bochum, Germanyg Ministerio de Ambiente, Montevideo, Uruguayh Instituto de Investigaciones Marinas y Costeras, Universidad Nacional de Mar del Plata, Mar del Plata, Argentinai United Nations Environment Programme, Washington DC, USAj European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC), Ispra, Italyk Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML), Faculty of Science, Leiden University, Leiden, The Netherlandsl Earth Systems and Global Change Group, Wageningen University & Research, Wageningen, The Netherlandsm Global Environment Monitoring Unit – GEMS/Water, Early Warning and Assessment Division, United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), Nairobi, KenyaElise C. Gallois is a postdoctoral research associate at UK Centre for Ecology and Hydrology and the University of Edinburgh. She is a data scientist and ecologist working as part of the uPcycle project to deliver the Global Lakes Explorer, a free and accessible data portal which contains nutrient emissions and impact data for over 40,000 lake catchments. Elise has expertise in spatial statistics, cross-sector communications, and data management. Philip Taylor is an Environmental Data Scientist at UKCEH, and leads in development of the uPcycle Global Phosphorus Dashboard. He specializes in lake catchment science, evaluating global freshwater conditions and recovery. He leads the UK Lakes Portal development, consolidating data for public access. With expertise in data analysis, coding languages, databases, and software. Will J. Brownlie is project manager of the uPcycle project and is a full-time staff member at UKCEH. Will previously managed the Our Phosphorus Future (OPF) initiative (www.opfglobal.com), consolidating global scientific evidence on phosphorus. He is lead editor of the OPF report. He contributes to the GEF/UNEP-UKCEH International Nitrogen Management System (INMS) project, developing the Nitrogen Measures Database and managing co-editor of the International Nitrogen Assessment. Will advises UNEP and national governments in various capacities on integrated nutrient sustainability. Maddalena Tigli is a data scientist working for the Atmospheric Chemistry and Effects department at UKCEH. Currently, she contributes to the development and management of some of the department’s web tools and datasets. Her interests lie in understanding the causes and the effects of climate change on natural, social, and economic systems. Erica Zaja is an Environmental Data Scientist at UKCEH with an MSc in Ecology from the University of Edinburgh and she is part of Components 1 and 4 of uPcycle. Erica works at the interface between data science, science communication and graphic design, and has a background in ecology and environmental science. Isabel H. Lewis is an Assistant Project Manager at UKCEH and is a member of the uPcycle’s coordination unit and design hub. She co-leads Component 4 of the project, focusing on the dissemination of outputs, external communications and the production of policy briefs. She contributes to reporting documents and facilitates the gender mainstreaming efforts. Issy has experience with research projects in both science communication and project coordination as well as a background in environmental science. Arthur H. W. Beusen obtained his PhD from Utrecht University (UU) in modelling the transport of nutrients from land to sea, which he has been involved since 1992. Arthur is considered an expert in designing, integrating, calibrating and evaluating complex environmental computer models, both on a local and global scale. At PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency and UU, he applies his expertise to advance the interface between policy and science thorough theoretical foundation of environmental issues while maintaining a clear and practical perspective on concrete applications. Valentina Rayén Escanilla Jaramillo is a renewable natural resources engineer with a diploma in Applied Geomatics. She is a CONICYT scholarship recipient for a Master’s degree in biological sciences. She has over 10 years of professional experience in developing studies related to the design, evaluation, monitoring, and enforcement of environmental quality standards and draft secondary standards. Valentina currently works at Ministerio Medio Ambiente in Chile. Pablo Andrés Etcharren Ulloa is a professional in charge of the Aquatic Ecosystems unit, of the Regional Ministerial Secretariat of the Environment of La Araucanía-Chile, coordinating the preparation of the Decontamination Plan for the Lake Villarrica basin, from the La Araucanía region. Pablo co-leads Component 3 of the uPcycle project, contributing to regional coordination with relevant actors, identification and analysis of water quality information from Lake Villarrica. Martina Floerke obtained her Ph.D. in Hydraulic Engineering and Water Management from the University of Kassel in 2002. She is now a Professor of Engineering Hydrology and Water Management at the Faculty of Civil and Environmental Engineering at Ruhr-University Bochum, where her research interests include cross-scale water modelling, scenario development and analysis, and evaluating trade-offs and synergies for achieving the UN SDGs. Mercedes Gelós is a natural resources specialist at the Ministry of Environment in Montevideo, Uruguay. Part of her work involves conducting integrated environmental assessments at the watershed scale, hydrological analysis, load analysis, integration of data from different sources, and implementation of water quality models to perform a macro-scale evaluation that allows us to weigh the pressures on natural systems and propose sustainable solutions. María de los Ángeles González Sagrario has a doctorate in Biology from the Universidad Nacional de Mar del Plata-CONICET in Buenos Aries, Argentina. Her research focuses on paleolimnology, shallow lakes, eutrophication, and the impacts of eutrophication on freshwater ecology. Ezra Kitson completed his Ph.D. in Environmental Chemistry at the University of Edinburgh. His Ph.D. research involved analysing the molecular and microbial composition of blanket bog peat in response to drainage and drain-blocking. During his Ph.D. he worked with large metagenomic and metabolomic datasets, which sparked his passion for data science. He is now a data scientist at UKCEH interested in creating data portals and applying machine learning algorithms to solve environmental data problems. Ivar Ledezma works at UNEP collaborating with IW: LEARN GEF projects. He has a Master of Science in Geo-Informatics and has worked as a GIS Consulting Engineer. Alice MacSporran is a freshwater fieldwork and laboratory technician at UKCEH, and has an MSc in Geographical Information Science from the University of Edinburgh. Cristina Martin Hernandez is an Information Systems and Data Scientist, at UKCEH. Within this role, she is a data centre operative in the Environmental Information Data Centre (EIDC) where she also develops and manages websites (including Drupal based websites) as well as online tools and applications. She also has expertise in processing of data and datasets. Christina’s research interests include environmental data (mainly atmospheric data) processing and transformation and how it changes over time and space. She has an interest in developing web tools that help users – including the general public and policy makers – to visualise data for decision making. Linda May has more than 45 years of experience as a freshwater ecologist. Her initial research focus was the population dynamics of zooplankton and their role as indicators of environmental quality. In recent years, this has shifted to the causes and effects of water quality problems in lakes. Her work now includes gathering the scientific evidence required to underpin the successful restoration of lakes and support their sustainable management. Sandra Mingarelli is a researcher at the European Commission Joint Research Centre. Her research interests include nutrient inputs to surface waters, ecological assessment methods in the European Union, and benthal algae and macrophyte assessments. Jose M. Mogollón is an Associate Professor at Leiden University in the Netherlands. José has worked over 11 years on quantifying and modeling Earth system processes and their responses to human pressures Sergio Felipe Sairafi Bazan is a professional in the Aquatic Ecosystems Department of the Ministry of the Environment of Chile. He has contributed to the development of the Decontamination Plan for the Villarrica Lake basin from Santiago and co-directs Component 3 of the uPcycle project. Sergio contributes to the Chilean national coordination of key actors and to the agenda of restoration and sustainable phosphorus management in lake basins. Maryna Strokal is an Associate Professor of Earth Systems and Global Change at Wageningen University. Her research interests include integrated modelling of pollutant flows from land to sea, and Scenario and Sensitivity Analyses. Ammanuel B. Tilahun has an MSc from IHE Delft Institute for Water Education in the Netherlands, and is now studying his Ph.D. in hydrology and water resources management at Ruhr University Bochum, Germany. His research interests include large scale hydrological and water quality monitoring and the application of machine learning for water management. Isabelle Vanderbeck has extensive experience in negotiating, formulating, and implementing technical assistance projects, primarily GEF-funded, collaborating with various partners including GEF agencies, UN Agencies, NGOs, government bodies, and academia. As an International Waters Task Manager at UNEP, she has spearheaded projects across 35 countries, addressing transboundary water issues and global challenges like blue forests valuation and carbon accounting. Isabelle’s work integrates climate adaptation, resource efficiency, and nature-based solutions, advancing conservation finance through innovative financing mechanisms in a ridge-to-reef context. Audric Vigier is a researcher at UKCEH, and manages several projects and work packages about tool development and modelling, around air quality and pollution, nitrogen management and soils. He is certified PRINCE2® 7 Foundation. He is an advanced R user, language he uses to develop Shiny apps and R packages, and handles and processes various environmental datasets, as well as runs short-range deposition models within the Air Quality Impacts and Responses group. He co-leads the UKCEH training “Mastering Environmental Data in R”. Stuart Warner works for United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) helping countries to report on SDG Indicator 6.3.2 (ambient water quality). Jinhui Zhou is a guest postdoctoral researcher at Leiden University in the Netherlands. Her research is focused on assessing the environmental impacts of future nitrogen dispersal across global watersheds. Bryan M. Spears serves as Director of the uPcycle project and works within UKCEH’s Freshwater Restoration and Sustainability Group, Edinburgh. He is co-chair of the International Society of Limnology Working Group on Lake Restoration and the United Nations Environment Programme coordinated World Water Quality Alliance (WWQA) WorkStream on Ecosystem Restoration. He works to raise awareness of the global need for lake restoration and supports countries and restoration programmes globally.
